messages:
jess: Heads up — main is red after merge of PR #842 (auth-rewrite). Build 6243 failing unit tests. CI shows failing test tests/tokenizer/test_edgecases.py::test_split_on_unicode. Link: https://ci.redwood.internal/builds/6243 :eyes:

ci-bot: Build 6243 — FAILED. Failed steps: unit-tests. Last 5 lines of log:
```
E   AssertionError: ['​'] != ['']
E   AssertionError: expected token stream without zero-width joiner
...
```

sam: @jess who merged #842? did the PR touch tokenizer code? can we rollback if needed?

jess: Merge author is @leah. PR changed normalization path for incoming text (NFKC). It did touch tokenizer/tokenize.py lines ~120-160. I haven't reverted anything yet. pinging owners.

leah: I'm in a meeting, got the ping. I pushed that normalization change to handle weird unicode in chat, worried about regressions — will jump on this in ~10m.

ravi: Can someone kick a rerun first, then I'll bisect if it repros consistently. If rerun is green we might have flake.

sam: Rerun triggered: https://ci.redwood.internal/builds/6244 (manual rerun by sam)

ci-bot: Build 6244 — FAILED (same test). Exact failure reproduced. Suspected regression range: commits 9cf3a2a -> 4f2b1e7.

ravi: OK I'll start a bisect between last green (commit abc123) and head (commit def456). Tagging @leah in case it's the change.

jess: If bisect points to leah's commit, please open a revert PR and mark it as emergency rollback. I'll coordinate with release.

leah: Understood — thanks. If it's my change I'll prepare a minimal fix for the tokenizer to preserve previous behavior for zero-width chars.

sam: Also option: quarantine test briefly to unblock main if bisect/fix will take longer. Thoughts?

ravi: I'll try bisect first. If it pins to a single commit, fix should be quick. If it's a combination, we can quarantine the test in pytest and add a follow-up to unquarantine after fix.

ci-bot: Bisect job queued: https://ci.redwood.internal/bisect/1823 — will post back with first failing commit.

jess: Thanks all. @leah please keep this thread posted when you have a workaround. :thumbsup:
